nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A nickel foam (3×2.5 cm²) was soaked into 2M HCl in an ultrasonic cleaner for 15 min. Then it was washed with deionized water and ethanol for 10 min and dried under N₂ flow.

nodes.name: CoNi-BDC@LDH one-pot synthesis
nodes.procedure: Terephthalic acid (166 mg) and urea (300 mg) were dissolved and sonicated in a mixture of 20 mL DMF and 20 mL deionized water. Then, Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (290 mg) and Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (290 mg) were added in the solution and sonicated for 30 min. The prepared solution was then transferred into a 40 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave together with an as-cleaned nickel foam (3 × 2.5 cm²) and heated in an oven at 120°C for 12 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the resultant sample was washed with deionized water and ethanol with ultrasonic cleaner for 15 min and dried at 80°C for 12 h in air to obtain CoNi-BDC@LDH.

nodes.name: Co-BDC synthesis (first step)
nodes.procedure: 290 mg of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O was first dissolved into 20 mL deionized water, and 155 mg of terephthalic acid was separately dissolved into 20 mL DMF. The two solutions were mixed and ultrasonicated for 30 min at room temperature. The mixed solution together with a cleaned Ni foam (3×2.5 cm²) was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated in an oven at 120°C for 12 h. The resultant samples were collected and rinsed with water for 30 min to obtain Co-BDC grown on a nickel foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoNi-BDC@LDH shows cuboid core-shell morphology with ~10 nm thick LDH nanoplates vertically grown on MOF substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the SEM images in Fig. 2a, 2b, and S1, CoNi-BDC@LDH manifests a cuboid shape... nanoplates with a thickness of ∼10 nm are vertically formed on the surface of MOF substrate, resulting in an overall core-shell structure where each cuboidal MOF is surrounded by numerous LDH nanoplates.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms core-shell structure in CoNi-BDC@LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images in Fig. 2c and S3 reassures the formation of a core-shell structure in CoNi-BDC@LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of CoNi-BDC@LDH displays lattice fringes with d-spacing 0.261 nm corresponding to (012) planes of CoNi-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Fig. 2d displays clear lattice fringes with an interplanar distance of 0.261 nm, corresponding to (012) planes of CoNi-LDH [26].

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental maps indicate Co, Ni, and O species uniformly dispersed throughout the CoNi-BDC@LDH structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental maps in Fig. 2e-2h indicate that Co, Ni, and O species are uniformly dispersed throughout the structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show LDH peaks at 40.2° and 46.8°; CoNi-BDC@LDH additionally shows α-Ni(OH)₂ (23.7°, 35.1°), β-Ni(OH)₂ (18.9°, 33.4°, 38.9°), and CoOOH (18.4°, 32.2°, 50.9°) peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks located at 40.2° and 46.8° are found in all samples and ascribed to the bimetallic Co and Ni-based LDH structure... CoNi-BDC@LDH exhibits additional peaks at 18.4°, 32.2° and 50.9°, which can be indexed to the (001), (100), and (102) planes of CoOOH (JCPDS# 30-0443).

nodes.characterization_summary: All BDC@LDH samples show isocyanate stretching at ∼2283 cm⁻¹ due to urea-aided BDC-LDH bonding and M-OH bending at ∼617, ∼570 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the FTIR spectra (Fig. S6b), all the BDC@LDH samples show the isocyanate (N = C = O) stretching mode (∼2283 cm⁻¹). Given the absence of isocyanate peak in CoNi-LDH... The peaks at ∼617 cm⁻¹ and ∼570 cm⁻¹ corresponding to Ni-OH and Co-OH bending vibrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: BDC@LDH samples show blue-shifted I_D (∼1418 cm⁻¹) and I_G (1618 cm⁻¹) bands with I_D/I_G = 1.01 for CoNi-BDC@LDH; M-O vibrations at 319, 455, 526 cm⁻¹ and NiOOH at 550 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectra (Fig. S7), all three BDC@LDH samples exhibit certain I_D and I_G band located at ∼1418 cm⁻¹ and 1618 cm⁻¹ respectively... The I_D/I_G ratio is calculated to be 1.01... The peaks at 319, 455 and 526 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the M-O vibrations... The 550 cm⁻¹ peak is attributed to NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoNi-BDC@LDH shows 41.5% O_β (oxygen defects), broader Ni³⁺ peak suggesting γ-NiOOH presence, and Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio of 0.87 vs 0.37 in CoNi-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is noted that the ratio of O_β (corresponding to oxygen defects) in CoNi-BDC@LDH is 41.5% higher than those of CoNi-LDH (27.8%)... The broader width of Ni³⁺ peak for CoNi-BDC@LDH suggests the existence of γ-NiOOH... CoNi-BDC@LDH has a Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio of 0.87 (Fig. S20b), significantly larger than CoNi-LDH (0.37).

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge shows stronger peak at ~530.6 eV (Co 3d/O 2p) and drop at 532.8 eV indicating oxygen vacancies in CoNi-BDC@LDH; higher Co³⁺/Co²⁺ and Ni valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the O K-edge spectra presented in Fig. 4b, the peak at ∼530.6 eV (Co 3d/O 2p) for CoNi-BDC@LDH is stronger... a distinct drop in the peak intensity at 532.8 eV... attributed to the formation of oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl = 169.9 μF cm⁻² for CoNi-BDC@LDH (vs 20.9 for CoNi-LDH, 20.2 for Co-BDC@LDH, 26.9 for Ni-BDC@LDH), yielding ECSA = 1.062 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated in Figs. S15 and S16, C_dl of CoNi-BDC@LDH is determined to be 169.9 μF cm⁻², which is significantly higher than those of CoNi-LDH (20.9 μF cm⁻²), Co-BDC@LDH (20.2 μF cm⁻²) and Ni-BDC@LDH (26.9 μF cm⁻²). The quantified ECSA of CoNi-BDC@LDH is 1.062 cm² (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi-operando ATR-FTIR shows O-O bond formation at 1090 cm⁻¹ during OER, intensifying with higher overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A zoomed-in ATR-FTIR in Fig. 5a shows the O-O bond (1090 cm⁻¹) formation during OER process... The intensification of O-O signal with a higher overpotential.

nodes.characterization_summary: C K-edge shows C1s→π* at ∼285.5 eV; O K-edge shows stronger Co 3d/O 2p peak at ∼530.6 eV and reduced intensity at 532.8 eV indicating oxygen vacancies in CoNi-BDC@LDH; higher Co³⁺/Co²⁺ and Ni³⁺ valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the O K-edge spectra presented in Fig. 4b, the peak at ∼530.6 eV (Co 3d/O 2p) for CoNi-BDC@LDH is stronger... a distinct drop in the peak intensity at 532.8 eV and a negative shift by ∼0.2 eV in CoNi-BDC@LDH is attributed to the formation of oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: At ≤1.43 V, Ni(OH)₂ peaks at 455, 526 cm⁻¹; at higher potentials, γ-NiOOH peaks emerge at ∼479, 557 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra are obtained at different overpotentials (Fig. S22). At a potential of 1.43 V or less, there are only two distinct peaks at 455 and 526 cm⁻¹, which correspond to Ni(OH)₂. At a higher potential, however, signals from slightly higher Raman shift values (∼479 and 557 cm⁻¹) start to emerge, which is ascribed to the formation of γ-NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: O-O bond formation at 1090 cm⁻¹ intensifies with increasing overpotential, indicating multi-metal site oxygen bridge formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A zoomed-in ATR-FTIR in Fig. 5a shows the O-O bond (1090 cm⁻¹) formation during OER process, which represents the establishment of oxygen bridge between multi-metal sites... The intensification of O-O signal with a higher overpotential.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio varies from 0.74 at 1.23 V to 0.29 at 1.43 V then 0.69 at 1.63 V; Co³⁺/Co²⁺ shows opposite trend, indicating collaborative Ni-Co contribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From XPS results (Fig. 5b), the relative Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio (Table S4) decreases from 0.74 at 1.23 V to 0.29 at 1.43 V and then increases to 0.69 at 1.63 V, while Co³⁺/Co²⁺ (Table S5) exhibits the opposite trend.
